text:
zoe: quick question about heatmap legibility when sampling is low — i'm trialing three treatments: hard bucket borders, softened blend, and a subtle pattern overlay on high bins. which is least likely to mislead non-power users? :thinking:

max: pattern overlay helps colorblind folks but can be visually noisy. i'd use pattern only in an accessibility mode or when the user enables "Show patterns" in prefs. otherwise softened blend + faint border.

leah: agree. also, when sample rate is low we should surface a tiny confidence indicator in the legend: e.g. "p95 • low confidence" with a tooltip explaining what that means. short tooltip copy: "Low sample density reduces percentile stability. Values are approximate."

own: UX note: keep the p95 line continuous for trend readability but add semi-opaque scatter markers at bucket centers when confidence >= threshold. hover shows exact bucket, count, and p95. keyboard focus moves between markers.

tara: accessibility nit: the bucket border color fails contrast at 1px thickness. options: thicker halo, increased opacity, or use `outline-offset` style. prefer halo to preserve hue semantics.

a11y-bot: recommended: stroke + 1px halo when contrast ratio < 4.5:1; ensure focusable controls have 3:1 target size and provide aria-labels for sliders. Also announce "Sample rate: X per second (low)" via aria-live when user pans time range.

zoe: love those requirements. interaction question: when a user toggles "Show bucket markers", should it be per-dashboard or global?

max: per-dashboard default but persist per-user if they toggle manually. that avoids surprising teammates. also add a keyboard shortcut hint in the tooltip e.g. "Press M to toggle markers (focused on heatmap)".

leah: microcopy proposal for the legend confidence badge: "p95 • approx" and tooltip: "Approximate 95th percentile — computed from few samples." keep it short.

own: implementation detail: backend can send `bucketConfidence` per bucket (low/med/high) and `estimatedSampleRate` for the view. client uses those to decide marker opacity and whether to show pattern overlay. we can start with thresholds: low < 20 samples, sampleRate < 0.4/sec.

tara: animation/accessibility: when markers appear/disappear due to density change, animate opacity with prefers-reduced-motion respected. and announce change: "Bucket markers enabled".

a11y-bot: keyboard plan: when heatmap is focused, left/right arrow moves focus between time slices; Enter opens tooltip for that slice (tooltip must be focusable). Add `aria-roledescription=\"interactive chart\"` to the container and `aria-describedby` linking to the confidence legend.

zoe: visual variant question: should we show bucket gridlines only at zoomed-in levels? e.g., when zoom > 15m per pixel show borders, otherwise hide. avoids clutter at wide ranges.

max: yes, dynamical gridlines make sense. plus add a toggle in the toolbar: "Show gridlines (zoom-only)". default off.

leah: analytics: track `marker_toggled`, `pattern_mode_enabled`, `confidence_tooltip_shown`, `sample_rate_aria_announced`. helps us measure confusion.

own: small CSS idea for pattern mode: use `background-image: linear-gradient(...), url(data:image/svg+xml;utf8,<svg>...)` so we can layer pattern only on high bins. fallback to color ramp when pattern data unavailable.

tara: copy for sample-rate pill: "sampled 0.32/s — low" with a question-mark tooltip linking to docs: "What does this mean?". Keep tooltip under 120 chars.

a11y-bot: ensure that the pill uses role=\"status\" and is announced when it appears. For screen reader users, include an extra line in the tooltip: "Use keyboard: Tab to open density controls."

zoe: summary / action items: Max to mock softened blend + optional pattern overlay (accessibility mode), Owen to prototype keyboard focus + marker traversal, Leah to draft short tooltip copy and confidence badge text, Tara to list contrast changes (halo rules). a11y-bot will paste checklist items in the design PR template.

max: i'll upload two gifs: (1) softened blend + p95 continuous with hover markers, (2) pattern overlay for a11y mode.

ow n: will do. leaning toward soften-by-default + opt-in pattern + per-dashboard persistent toggles.

zoe: thanks all — i'll slot this into Friday's design review. please add mock files to the thread when ready. :sparkles:
